label: Finishing a resin kit
blurb: The order is not a preference. Resin punishes a step done out of sequence weeks later, when the paint lifts.

nodes.label: Flash removal
nodes.blurb: Trimming the casting seams and pour stubs. Resin dust is the part nobody warns a collector about, so wet sand it.

nodes.label: Pinning
nodes.blurb: Brass rod and a pin vise through both halves of a joint. Resin is heavy and a butt joint will fail, usually while somebody is holding it.

nodes.label: Degreasing
nodes.blurb: An overnight soak, a rinse and an ultrasonic clean to remove mould release. It is invisible, and skipping it lifts the paint weeks later.

nodes.label: Priming
nodes.blurb: A light mist coat, then a heavier one. The first primer layer shows every flaw that bare resin was hiding.

nodes.label: Pinhole repair
nodes.blurb: Bubbles that extend below the surface, so filling the top does not fix them. This is where the time actually goes.

nodes.label: Skin tones
nodes.blurb: The base coat that decides how the whole figure reads. Airbrushed in thin layers, warm in the shadows rather than grey.

nodes.label: Face and eyes
nodes.blurb: The single hardest step, and it has to happen before the hair goes on because the hair blocks access permanently.

nodes.label: Hair assembly
nodes.blurb: Puttied seams, then reprimed and repainted locally. Assembly and painting stop being separate stages here.

nodes.label: Gloss and flat
nodes.blurb: Gloss to carry a wash, flat to finish. Two different jobs that people mistake for one preference.

edges.note: The one absolute prerequisite in the build. Mould release film is invisible and paint over it fails later.
Paint the face first. Once the hair is on you cannot reach it again.
